item.title: Shell
item.description:
A POSIX shell for WASI containers, in pure Go, built for GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm: go-wasmcontainers/shell. It is what will make shell-form commands work: RUN a && b in a Containerfile, wctr run IMAGE sh -c '…', and wctr exec -it CONTAINER sh.

Status: the guest side exists; the engine side is in progress. A WebAssembly module cannot start another program: Go’s port has no fork or exec, and WASI preview 1 has no process calls. So the shell uses a small subset of WASIX, in WASIX’s own import module (wasix_32v1): proc_spawn3, proc_join, fd_pipe, proc_id, proc_parent, tty_get and tty_set, and nothing else (no fork, exec, threads or signals). A host that implements the subset is needed: wasmer, which the tests use, or this engine once its host side is done. Nothing here runs in wctr yet, and wctr exec does not exist yet; a base image is also in progress.

  • wasix: //go:wasmimport bindings for the subset, with a Go API.
  • sh: the mvdan.cc/sh v3.14.1 interpreter (patched with one change: a pipe function, since upstream’s os.Pipe is ENOSYS on wasip1), whose external commands start with proc_spawn3.

sh does pipelines, redirections, here-documents, command substitution, cd, exported variables, $?, set -e/-u/-x/-f/-a, exec, sh -c, sh file and an interactive prompt on a TTY. By design of the subset it has no signals, no job control and no process substitution.
